title: Property R∞ for some spherical and affine Artin–Tits groups
extended_summary:
This paper studies the Reidemeister number problem for automorphisms of certain Artin–Tits groups, asking when every automorphism has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes, i.e. property R∞. The authors focus on irreducible Artin–Tits groups of spherical types An, Bn, D4, I2(m), their pure subgroups, and affine types \u007eAn−1 and \u007eCn.

The main approach is group-theoretic and geometric: the authors identify suitable central quotients of these groups with finite-index subgroups of extended mapping class groups of punctured surfaces. For an arbitrary automorphism ϕ, they construct an associated extension Gϕ and use its action on the curve complex of the relevant surface. Combining non-elementary hyperbolic actions, Delzant's lemma, and known results on twisted conjugacy in hyperbolic groups, they show that the coset corresponding to ϕ contains infinitely many conjugacy classes, which implies R(ϕ)=∞.

The paper does not involve human participants, classrooms, or an educational intervention; it is a theoretical result in geometric group theory. The main conclusion is that the specified spherical and affine Artin–Tits groups, along with several pure and central quotient variants, all have property R∞. The authors also recover and generalize a recent result for pure braid groups as a special case.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a mathematics research paper on group theory and twisted conjugacy, not an empirical education study. It does not evaluate any instructional technology, AI intervention, or learner outcome.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention, comparison group, or K-12 outcome is studied, so there is no measurable educational impact to code.
